To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the production of humified organic carbon from low-rank coal through bacterial solubilizing activity is a potential strategy for the recovery of organic matter from coal mining waste.

(a) the bacterial strains isolated in this work were capable of solubilizing LRC and producing HS in a liquid growth culture, (b) the HA produced by B mycoides were characterized by an elemental composition, an IR spectrum and a degree of aromatic condensations similar to those of HA extracted from coal with NaOH, (c) these bacterial strains could be exploited to improve the content humified organic matter (HOM) in soils.
The biotransformation of low rank coal by bacterial strains isolated from coal wastes can lead to humic acid production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biodegradation of LRC and the production of HS through the use of bacterial strains isolated in coal mining environments.
the production of humified organic substances from coal waste through bacterial solubilisation.
the biotransformation of LRC into HS by bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of these bacteria for the production of HA from coal wastes is promising, although further studies are needed to optimize the process and evaluate its economic viability.

this work provides the first report of the production of humified organic carbon through the bacterial solublization of LRC, which is an important step towards the development of new strategies for the management of coal waste.
these bacteria can produce humic acids in vitro from low rank coal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bacterial strains studied can be used to improve the content in humified organic matter of soils, thus increasing the fertility of the soils and their ability to sequester CO2 from the atmosphere.
we are able to produce humic substances from coal wastes by using coal solubilizing bacteria, and these HS are able to improve the content in humified organic matter of soils.
the use of these bacteria in coal-solubizing processes is a viable and sustainable alternative to chemical extraction for the production of HS, which can be used to improve the quality of soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biotransformed coal and the humic acids produced can be used to improve soil fertility and to remediate contaminated soils.
the biodegradation of low rank coal by bacteria may represent a new way of humic acid production.
the biotransformation of LRC by bacteria is a promising approach to produce HS for agricultural and environmental applications.
